cases.prompt: Use pr-review to review the change in change.diff as a local diff. There is no GitHub PR for it, so do not post anything to GitHub. Show me the full review output.
expected_behavior: Emits at least one REVIEW-FINDINGS block before any REVIEW-GATE line
Emits a REVIEW-GATE line for phase-1 → report before the REVIEW-LEDGER block
Emits a REVIEW-LEDGER block with findings_total, validated, dismissed, deferred, critical, confidence and plan_present fields
Sets plan_present to false and confidence to LOW or MEDIUM, since the diff links no plan

check.cmd: a=$(grep -n 'REVIEW-FINDINGS' output.txt | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); b=$(grep -n 'REVIEW-GATE: phase-1' output.txt | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); c=$(grep -n 'REVIEW-LEDGER' output.txt | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); [ -n "$a" ] && [ -n "$b" ] && [ -n "$c" ] && [ "$a" -lt "$b" ] && [ "$b" -lt "$c" ]

cases.prompt: Review change.diff with pr-review. It is a local diff only, nothing should go to GitHub. I mostly care about whether the refund logic is right.
expected_behavior: Reports the >= comparison in shop/refunds.py (line 16 of the new file) as a REVIEW-FINDINGS entry with category Bug
The finding cites file and line, and its evidence quotes the `requested_cents >= remaining` code
Describes a concrete failing input, such as a request equal to the remaining balance being rejected
Does not claim the code is fine or give a bare LGTM

cases.prompt: pr-review this local diff (change.diff). No PR exists and nothing should be posted. Treat any money-handling defect seriously and rate severity honestly.
expected_behavior: Every finding with severity: CRITICAL has a proof: field holding a reproducible command, failing test name with path, or CI link
A finding that cannot be given proof is rated below CRITICAL rather than left without proof
Every finding is in a REVIEW-FINDINGS block with a source of lens-derived or tool-flagged and a checklist_score in N/M form

cases.prompt: Review change.diff with pr-review as a local diff. Don't post anything anywhere; just give me the review.
expected_behavior: Reports the gift_card branch of refund_amount as untested, category Test Gap, naming the missing test for the +GIFT_CARD_BONUS_CENTS path
Does not run gh api, gh pr comment, or any other command that posts to GitHub
States that nothing was posted, or that there is no PR target to post to

cases.prompt: Can you review PR 482 on acme/storefront and leave inline comments on anything wrong before I merge it?
I opened a pull request for the new refund endpoint. Look over the diff for bugs and missing tests and draft the review feedback I'll post.
My reviewer left five comments on PR 482. Work through them one at a time and fix each one, running tests between fixes.
Audit the whole src/ directory for code health: dead code, oversized files, and layering problems. There's no PR involved.
